failures.assertion: Names at least one condition for pausing or stopping the joint session
failures.evidence: The only contingency is "If it stalls: go back to the shared goal of no repeat of a 70-minute rollback", which redirects the session rather than naming a condition to pause or stop it.

failures.assertion: The session plan uses the facts table from facilitation.md (an agreed column and a disputed column, with no third column for what really happened)
failures.evidence: The plan admits "I can't read it in this session" and uses its own three-column table, "Observed facts (checkable) | Disputed | Interpretations", which adds a third column and mixes agreed points with unverified items like "Luis's channel message exists".

failures.assertion: Gives a check-in agenda that asks what is working, what is not, whether to adjust, and whether to close the topic
failures.evidence: The agenda covers "Status of agreed actions," "How it's working," and "Going forward," but never explicitly asks what is not working or whether to close the overall topic; only the 28 April record has "If it's resolved, close it."

failures.assertion: Keeps the prep short and does not hand over the full multi-part worksheet
failures.evidence: The output has seven numbered sections, from "### 1. Readiness check (30 seconds)" through "### 7. After (within 1 working day)", including defensiveness handling and a follow-up note template, which amounts to the full multi-part worksheet rather than a short prep.

failures.assertion: Ends with a written opening line the user can say first
failures.evidence: A written opening line appears mid-document in section 3 ("On [day], the change to [service] was merged without me being looped in..."), but the output ends with the "Pocket version: facts → impact → ... → follow up in writing" summary, not the opening line.

failures.assertion: Gives the person a choice and a named time, keeping it a pause rather than an end to the conversation
failures.evidence: The times are named and "Nothing gets decided while we're out" keeps it a pause, but the manager picks the option "depending on how upset they are," and neither script asks the person to choose between twenty minutes and tomorrow.

failures.assertion: Describes breathing in and out steadily with a count of about 1 to 5 each and no breath hold
failures.evidence: The output uses unequal counts plus a double inhale, "In through your nose for **4** counts... Out slowly through pursed lips for **6** counts" after "take one more short sip of air," not a steady 1-to-5 in and out.

failures.assertion: Says that at least five minutes is the recommended length and that what the user can do now is the shorter version
failures.evidence: The output only says "It fits in five minutes" and offers a "2-minute breathing reset" without saying that five minutes or more is the recommended length or calling this the shorter version.

failures.assertion: Offers one technique rather than a full wellness routine (no sleep, exercise or mindfulness advice)
failures.evidence: It stacks several techniques: "Two 'sighs' to start," an extended exhale, a grounding step ("name three things you can see"), a mindfulness-style cue ("notice it and go back to counting"), and a separate "60 seconds before you walk in" routine.
